source_name: НКЦПФР — Регуляторна діяльність (Regulatory activities, draft acts & consultations)
why_relevant: Section carrying plans for preparation of draft regulatory acts and published drafts. This is where forward-looking regulatory burden (and consultation comment deadlines) appears before adoption.

source_name: НКЦПФР — «Ключові рішення НКЦПФР від DD-MM-YYYY» news series
why_relevant: Recurring, near-weekly summary of adopted Commission decisions with resolution numbers. Highest-frequency signal of new obligations on capital-market participants; predictable URL pattern makes it cheap to monitor. English mirror exists (/en/kliuchovi-rishennia-nktspfr-...).

source_name: НКЦПФР — Аналітична довідка про роботу Комісії та стан ринків капіталу (quarterly analytical reports, PDF)
why_relevant: Quarterly official statistics and enforcement/licensing activity on capital and organised commodity markets — gives supervisory intensity trend, not just individual acts. PDFs are served from a predictable wp-content path.

source_name: АМКУ — Контроль за концентраціями та узгодженими діями (merger-control landing page)
why_relevant: Procedural hub: how to file for concentration clearance, fees, and the statutory review phases. Source of the deadline architecture (Phase I/Phase II) that binds bank M&A and PSP acquisitions.

source_name: АМКУ — «Інформація про рішення та розпорядження АМКУ» decision bulletin series
why_relevant: Dated bulletins listing granted concentration permits, including named bank transactions (e.g. АТ «БАНК ІНВЕСТИЦІЙ ТА ЗАОЩАДЖЕНЬ», ПАТ «ВіЕс Банк»). Best available public trace of who is consolidating in Ukrainian banking/payments.

source_name: АМКУ — payments/acquiring market investigations and market studies (PrivatBank / Oschadbank acquiring & interchange)
why_relevant: AMCU has run a multi-year abuse-of-dominance investigation into merchant acquiring and interchange involving the two largest state banks, and publishes draft amendments to the Положення про концентрацію. Directly shapes PSP/acquirer economics — a competition-side regulatory risk invisible on NBU domains.

source_name: Держфінмоніторинг — Форми обліку і подання інформації (reporting forms & technical specs)
why_relevant: The exact page where reporting form versions (1-ФМ, 2-ФМ, 4-ФМ …), file-format specifications and their changeover dates are published. Format changes create hard IT deadlines for every bank and PSP.

source_name: Держфінмоніторинг — типологічні дослідження та методичні матеріали (typologies / guidance PDFs)
why_relevant: Typology studies define red-flag indicators that supervised banks are formally expected to incorporate into risk models; the Ministry of Economy has issued instructions telling reporting entities to take them into account. De facto quasi-binding guidance.

source_name: sdfm.gov.ua — legacy SFMS website
why_relevant: Predecessor domain of the SFMS, still referenced as carrying official information and historical archives (annual reports, older typologies) that may not have migrated to fiu.gov.ua. Useful for backfill.

source_name: Міністерство фінансів України — сторінка Держфінмоніторингу (SFMS coordination page)
why_relevant: SFMS is coordinated through the Minister of Finance, and the binding AML reporting procedures are issued as MoF orders (наказ Мінфіну), not SFMS acts. The MoF page is the pointer that connects the FIU to the ministry that actually issues its normative acts.

source_name: Державна регуляторна служба України (DRS) — аналіз проєктів регуляторних актів
why_relevant: Cross-authority gatekeeper for regulatory acts: DRS reviews and publishes analyses of draft regulatory acts from many bodies, including competition and financial-sector regulators. A single choke point that surfaces drafts you would otherwise have to find on each supervisor's own site.

source_name: data.gov.ua — Держфінмоніторинг as data publisher (open datasets)
why_relevant: Machine-readable datasets published by the SFMS on the national open-data portal — the only structured, licence-clear route to SFMS material given that fiu.gov.ua resists automated fetching.

source_name: ПАРД — Професійна асоціація учасників ринків капіталу та деривативів
why_relevant: SRO-status association that publishes fast, plain-language readouts of NSSMC decisions and SFMS reports, plus joint industry letters opposing draft rules. Excellent early-warning and sentiment layer, and it mirrors regulator documents that are hard to fetch directly.

source_name: УАІБ — Українська асоціація інвестиційного бізнесу
why_relevant: Second SRO in the capital-markets space; co-signs industry submissions to NSSMC (e.g. on squeeze-out) and hosts localized regulator documents. Complements PARD for consultation-stage intelligence.

source_name: Академія фінансового моніторингу / finmonitoring.in.ua
why_relevant: Training/practitioner outlet in the SFMS orbit that reports portal changes, new forms and compliance obligations in operational language. Useful as a low-friction mirror when fiu.gov.ua blocks automated access.

source_name: Ukrainian competition-law firm merger-control guides (Asters, VKP, Chambers, GCR)
why_relevant: Annually refreshed English-language restatements of AMCU thresholds, the special one-tenth-of-assets rule for banks, filing timelines and Phase I/II statistics. Fastest way to get a defensible baseline of Ukrainian merger-clearance burden on banks without parsing Ukrainian statute.

source_name: Держпродспоживслужба (State Service on Food Safety and Consumer Protection) — financial-services consumer pages
why_relevant: Frequently assumed to be the consumer-protection supervisor for banks, but its own publications state that supervision of banks' compliance with financial-services consumer-protection and financial advertising law sits with the NBU. Worth tracking mainly as a boundary/jurisdiction marker and for general consumer-law changes that spill into retail finance.

source_name: CSIRT-NBU — Cyber Defence Centre of the National Bank of Ukraine (cyber.bank.gov.ua)
why_relevant: The NBU's own CSIRT/cyber defence centre portal for banks and, since 2024-2025, non-bank financial service providers. Publishes incident-reporting obligations (significant cyber incident notification within 72h to csirt-nbu@bank.gov.ua plus a final report within one month), guidance, threat notices and sectoral cyber requirements. It is the single operational bridge between NBU information-security rules and SSSCIP/CERT-UA.

source_name: NBU news — consultation launches on information security / cyber defence rules (bank.gov.ua news)
why_relevant: NBU announces the opening of each public consultation here, with the draft PDF attached and the transition period stated (e.g. six months for financial service providers to align). Best early-warning signal for upcoming security obligations and their deadlines.

source_name: NBU Resolution No.143 of 09.12.2025 — Regulation on information security and cyber defence measures by financial service providers (zakon.rada.gov.ua)
why_relevant: The current binding rulebook for non-bank financial service providers (finance companies, insurers, credit unions, pawnshops), in force from mid-December 2025 with a compliance horizon reported as end-2026. DORA-aligned. A hard-deadline document that drives procurement of security tooling.

source_name: NBU Resolution No.69 of 27.06.2025 — Critical infrastructure of the financial sector (amending Regulation No.178 on cyber defence in the banking system)
why_relevant: Unifies criteria for designating critical infrastructure objects across the financial sector and amends the 2022 banking cyber-defence regulation. Determines which banks/PSPs fall under the heavier SSSCIP-linked obligations.

source_name: NBU Regulation No.178 of 12.08.2022 — Organisation of cyber defence in the banking system of Ukraine (ipLex mirror)
why_relevant: The core banking cyber-defence regulation and companion to the 2017 information-security regulation; defines critical infrastructure objects in the banking system and incident-reporting duties. ipLex is a usable mirror when rada.gov.ua is rate-limited.

source_name: NBU Resolution No.95 of 28.09.2017 — Regulation on information security measures in the banking system (zakon.rada.gov.ua)
why_relevant: The baseline ISMS regulation for Ukrainian banks (ISO 27001-style requirements, phased implementation). A March-2025 draft replacement was published for consultation, so the pair (in-force act + draft successor) shows the direction of travel and future deadlines.

source_name: NBU Resolution No.24 of 2025 — amendments to NBU acts on information security and cyber defence
why_relevant: Amendment package touching several NBU information-security/cyber acts at once; the kind of omnibus change that silently resets compliance dates for banks and PSPs.

source_name: SSSCIP / Administration of the State Service of Special Communications and Information Protection (cip.gov.ua)
why_relevant: The cybersecurity regulator outside the financial vocabulary: sets and approves basic, sectoral and target security profiles, runs security authorisation, hosts CERT-UA, and issues the general cyber-defence requirements for critical information infrastructure that banks fall under. Publishes orders and methodological recommendations as PDF attachments via its CMS.

source_name: CSIRT of the State Scientific and Research Institute of Cybersecurity Technologies and Information Protection — regulatory framework pages
why_relevant: A curated, maintained index of Ukraine's cyber-defence and critical-infrastructure legal framework, including a dedicated page on the CI-protection legal base. Excellent snowball hub for orders and methodological recommendations that never surface in financial-regulator searches.

source_name: CERT-UA — government computer emergency response team (cip.gov.ua/CERT-UA channels)
why_relevant: Issues the operational advisories and UAC-cluster reports that shape bank/PSP defensive obligations; UAC-0050 and UAC-0006 are explicitly financially motivated clusters targeting accountants' payment workflows. Advisories often precede regulatory tightening.

source_name: Law of Ukraine No.4336-IX of 27.03.2025 — amendments on information protection and cyber defence of state information resources and CII objects
why_relevant: The framework statute that reformatted Ukraine's cyber-defence system, replacing the old KSZI/complex-protection paradigm with security profiles and security authorisation. Everything SSSCIP now imposes on CII operators, banks included, derives from it.
